items.title: Audience & Content Growth Lead, SMB Ads
items.description: About the Team OpenAI is building the next generation of advertising for an AI-powered world. As AI changes how people discover information, explore possibilities, and make decisions, we believe this presents a huge opportunity for small and medium-sized businesses to connect with customers in new ways. The SMB Ads Marketing team is building this opportunity from the ground up. We define how businesses discover OpenAI’s advertising platform, become successful advertisers, and grow their investment over time. Working closely with Product, Ads Engineering, Data Science, and Sales, we combine customer insight, rigorous experimentation, and fast execution to turn early opportunities into scalable growth. About the Role We are looking for an Audience & Content Growth Lead to build the global content and education programs that inspire, inform and engage SMB advertisers. This is a zero-to-one opportunity to shape how small businesses discover and understand advertising with OpenAI. You will turn customer needs, product capabilities and advertiser success stories into compelling content—from webinars and educational video series to case studies, industry-specific playbooks and creator-led programs. The role combines two areas of ownership: developing content specifically for SMB audiences and building effective ways to distribute it. You will lead programs directly while partnering with teams that own web, social, lifecycle marketing, growth and regional channels to reach the right audiences at scale. Success means building an engaged SMB audience and helping businesses move from awareness to understanding, confidence and action. In This Role, You Will - Set the global SMB content strategy and editorial roadmap, grounded in customer needs, industry priorities, and advertiser maturity. - Create compelling customer stories, case studies, vertical playbooks, guides, videos, and thought leadership that make advertising accessible and actionable. - Launch repeatable education programs through webinars, expert sessions, workshops, and on-demand learning that help businesses get started and improve their advertising. - Grow audiences through owned, shared, and partner channels. Build distribution plans with web, social, growth, lifecycle, and regional teams. - Develop creator-, expert-, and customer-led programs that combine credible education, authentic storytelling, and relevant audience reach. - Scale programs across markets with regional teams. Adapt formats, languages, customer stories, and distribution to local needs. - Lead editorial planning, production, agencies, and creative contributors. Maintain quality, accessibility, and accuracy, using AI to support content creation, adaptation, and reuse. - Measure audience quality, engagement, learning, and advertiser action with Growth, Lifecycle, and Data Science. Use experiments and feedback to improve content and distribution. You Might Thrive in This Role If You - Bring 10+ years of experience in content marketing, audience development, or customer education, including programs for SMBs or advertisers. - Demonstrate ownership of content creation and distribution that grows relevant audiences and drives customer action. - Translate complex products into clear, engaging content through strong editorial judgment and storytelling. - Build repeatable programs across formats such as webinars, video, customer stories, vertical playbooks, and creator-led content. - Lead cross-functional and partner-led distribution, aligning teams around shared priorities and measurable outcomes. - Measure learning, intent, and business impact alongside content consumption. - Adapt global programs to different markets and audiences in partnership with regional teams. - Combine strategy with hands-on writing, editing, creative briefing, and program execution. Preferred Experience - Bring experience with advertising platforms, marketplaces, or technology businesses serving SMBs. - Build on experience in advertiser education, customer advocacy, creator partnerships, or partner-distributed learning. - Draw on experience in both established technology organizations and startup or zero-to-one environments. Workplace & Location - San Francisco, CA. This role requires a hybrid schedule with an in office requirement from Monday - Wednesday. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. items.title: Customer Marketing Lead, Startups Program
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We're hiring a Customer Marketing, Startups Lead to own our strategy for how Anthropic shows up in market with the startups building on Claude, from early-stage founders to our largest AI-native customers. You'll figure out how we can help startups grow, and find creative ways to amplify their stories to inspire more companies to do the same. This is a role for someone who has led marketing at a startup and knows what founders need. You'll work closely with our Startups account teams to decide where co-marketing will create real value for both the startup and Anthropic. For the startups we prioritize together, you'll work directly with founders and their teams as a marketing partner on channels and the joint messages we take to market. Many of these companies don't have big marketing teams yet, so you'll also advise them on storytelling and growth. This role is deeply cross-functional. You'll work with Startups Sales leadership, Startup Partnerships, Segment Marketing, Field Marketing, Partner Marketing, Product Marketing, Brand, Comms, and Legal. You'll set direction with senior leaders here and at our customers, and lead a team of startups customer marketers while staying hands-on in the work yourself. Key responsibilities Own startups co-marketing, including deciding which startups and moments are worth investing in Be a marketing partner to founders and CEOs on channels and joint messaging, and advise companies without built-out marketing teams on storytelling and growth Partner with Startups Sales leadership and embed in the deal flow so you can see deals coming and plan how co-marketing can support them Work with account teams on the market development funds (MDF) in startup contracts, and own how those funds are deployed Build programs that bring co-marketing to hundreds of startups, beyond our top accounts Set the bar for startup storytelling and find creative ways to amplify those stories, from case studies and founder films to content on how startups use Claude Find opportunities to bring startups into Anthropic's launches and campaigns Work with Startup Partnerships and Segment Marketing on the Claude Startups program and our relationships with VCs and accelerators Build a feedback loop that shares what founders care about with Anthropic's leadership and GTM teams Lead and develop a team of startups customer marketers Minimum qualifications Have been a trusted advisor to founders and CEOs, and enjoy working closely with them Know when co-marketing will create real value for both companies, and when it won't Are a strong storyteller and writer who can tell what makes a founder's story worth telling Have a deep read on what startups want, and can quickly see what will help a small marketing team most Have led senior cross-functional work across Sales, Marketing, Product, and Comms Can influence teams you don't own, and are comfortable presenting to executives Have strong taste and judgment, and can say no, including to senior leaders Are a player-coach, comfortable setting direction for a team and doing the hands-on work yourself Are comfortable with technical products and can talk credibly with technical founders Can keep up with a fast pace Already use Claude in your own work Care about Anthropic's mission Preferred qualifications Have 12+ years in B2B marketing, including senior marketing leadership at a startup, like CMO, VP of Marketing, or Head of Marketing Been a founder or an early marketing hire at a startup Worked in AI, developer tools, or another technical category Worked at a company that sells to startups Built relationships with VCs and accelerators A network of founders and startup marketing leaders Run co-marketing programs with real budget behind them Role-specific policy: For this role, we expect all staff to be able to work from our San Francisco or New York offices at least 2 days a week, though we encourage you to apply even if you might need some flexibility for an interim period of time for relocation. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $400,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Power Generation Design Engineer, Electrical & Mechanical
items.description: About the Team OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness. The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed. About the Role We are seeking a Power Generation Design Engineer to help design and integrate generation plants and balance-of-plant systems for large AI data center campuses. This role spans electrical and mechanical systems, including generation equipment, campus and grid interfaces, fuel and auxiliary systems, cooling, controls, and data center loads. The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in either electrical or mechanical engineering, along with the cross-disciplinary judgment to evaluate how the full plant operates as an integrated system. You will establish technical requirements, assess vendor and EPC solutions, resolve design interfaces, and carry systems from concept through commissioning and validated operation. Travel: 50% Responsibilities - Develop and review generation-plant basis-of-design documents, design criteria, specifications, diagrams, calculations, and reference architectures. - Define and coordinate interfaces among generation equipment, substations, campus distribution, grid connections, fuel systems, cooling, controls, and data center loads. - Evaluate generation technologies and operating modes, including grid-connected and islanded operation, synchronization, load sharing, black start, and restoration. - Lead or review discipline-specific engineering analyses. Electrical studies may include load flow, short circuit, arc flash, protection coordination, transient, grounding, and motor starting. Mechanical analyses may include thermal performance, hydraulics, pressure drop, ventilation, vibration, acoustics, and heat recovery. - Review OEM and EPC proposals, equipment ratings and performance data, operating envelopes, failure modes, test plans, maintenance strategies, and lifecycle tradeoffs. - Translate data center load profiles and operating requirements into generation-system capacity, redundancy, performance, and control requirements. - Coordinate with electrical, mechanical, controls, CSA, fuel, utility, environmental, fire-protection, and data center engineering teams to resolve design and delivery interfaces. - Support procurement, factory acceptance testing, construction, startup, energization, commissioning, performance testing, and root-cause investigations. - Develop repeatable technical standards and reference designs that improve reliability, maintainability, and deployment speed across future projects. Qualifications - 8+ years of engineering experience in power generation, utilities, industrial systems, microgrids, oil and gas, or mission-critical infrastructure. - Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field. - Deep technical expertise in either electrical power systems or mechanical/process systems, with experience collaborating across the other discipline. - Electrical expertise may include generators, transformers, HV/MV switchgear, protection and controls, grounding, auxiliary power, grid interconnection, and power-system studies. - Mechanical expertise may include rotating equipment, fuel and fluid systems, piping, heat transfer, cooling, ventilation, lubrication, water treatment, exhaust, and mechanical auxiliaries. - Experience evaluating OEM data, equipment performance, operating scenarios, failure modes, and maintenance requirements. - Experience carrying engineering designs through construction, startup, commissioning, and operational validation. - Ability to communicate technical risks and tradeoffs clearly across engineering, vendors, construction, and operations. Preferred Skills - Professional Engineer license. - Experience with gas turbines, reciprocating engines, battery systems, combined heat and power, heat recovery, or hybrid generation plants. - Familiarity with relevant codes and standards, including NEC, NFPA, IEEE, NERC, ASME, API, ASHRAE, and utility requirements. - Proficiency with applicable analysis or modeling tools, such as ETAP, PSCAD, PSS/E, SKM, EasyPower, process simulation, hydraulic modeling, or CFD. - Experience supporting high-density data center loads and rapidly changing AI compute demand. items.title: Lead Product Designer, Growth (Mobile)
items.description: In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. We’ve scaled beyond the millions of people using Perplexity every day for research, shopping, investing and curiosity into a new paradigm of using AI to transform knowledge into action. ABOUT THE ROLE Perplexity is looking for an experienced Lead Product Designer to own mobile design for Growth. You'll shape the experiences that bring Perplexity to as many people as possible on the device they reach for first, making software that feels like the future but can be understood and used by anyone in the world today. Growth design has its own craft and nuance, and so does mobile. You'll own the highest-leverage moments in the mobile user journey: first-run onboarding and activation, consumer acquisition surfaces, conversion flows, paywalls and pricing, the nudges and upsells that drive adoption of new products and features, and the retention loops that turn first-time users into daily ones. This is design where a few pixels, a single step, or the timing of a transition can move real numbers, so you'll pair a high craft bar with rigorous experimentation, letting real data guide the work. You'll do that in the real material: prototyping on device, writing SwiftUI in Xcode, and putting up your own PRs. You care about clarity, craft, details, and delight as much as you care about growth and impact. This role is deeply cross-functional: you'll partner closely with our Growth, Product Marketing, mobile engineering, and brand design teams, and you care about everything it takes to make a product great: product, interaction, growth, copywriting, engineering, and marketing. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Lead mobile product design for Growth across the full lifecycle: acquisition, activation, retention, monetization, and enterprise expansion - Design first-run and onboarding experiences that feel native to the platform and get users to value as fast as possible - Craft conversion and upsell flows for mobile, including paywalls, pricing, and plan comparison - Design growth experiences for an AI-native product, getting people to their first great answer fast and helping them discover new capabilities like Computer - Bring the Perplexity brand to life in our growth surfaces through cinematic motion, visual design, and interaction detail - Prototype on device early and often, using real code to answer questions static mocks can't - Write SwiftUI and put up your own PRs, working alongside mobile engineers to close the gap between the design and what ships - Partner closely with Growth and Product Marketing on positioning, messaging, and funnel strategy - Design and run experiments, using data and real usage to drive decisions and measure impact - Explore what new platform capabilities and form factors make possible for growth - Think about how to go from 0→1 but also how to make your decisions scale well - Contribute to process so we're always shipping changes you're proud of, as often as possible WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Experience designing consumer or prosumer products, with a strong track record of shipping native mobile apps - Deep fluency in iOS: platform conventions, navigation patterns, gestures, system components, and what's new each year - A solid understanding of growth nuances: onboarding, activation, acquisition, conversion, upsells, paywalls, pricing, and retention - A data-informed approach, fluent in experimentation, funnels, and metrics, and comfortable learning from usage - Excellent visual, UI, interaction, and motion skills, with a knack for bringing a brand to life in product without getting in the way of use - Comfort prototyping on device, working in Xcode with SwiftUI, and putting up your own PRs in a production codebase - An excellent communicator who can tell a clear story from data and design rationale to team members and leadership - You care about shipping great software more than anything else - Comfort with a high level of autonomy and ambiguity, and the craft to be seen as a peer lead by the rest of the design team - 5+ years of industry experience NICE TO HAVE - Experience designing for Android or working in Jetpack Compose (we design iOS-first, but Android is in scope) - Fluency with motion tools such as Rive, Lottie, or After Effects - You've already been exploring or prototyping interactions for foldables like iPhone Duo NOTES FOR CANDIDATES - Please submit your portfolio with your application.

You'll design how Perplexity lives on the device people carry everywhere, and how that device works with everything else they use: their Mac, their Windows PC, their Linux machine, and the agents doing work on their behalf. Native & Mobile is one team covering every platform we build for. Our agents increasingly run for minutes or hours, on your computer or in the cloud, and the phone becomes the place you start that work, follow its progress, step in when it needs you, and pick up the result. You'll design that relationship between devices so it feels like one product, not a set of separate apps. The best mobile work here goes deep on the platform. You'll design experiences that take full advantage of what each device can do: notifications, Live Activities and the Dynamic Island, widgets, voice, Shortcuts and App Intents, share and system extensions, and their Android counterparts. You'll prototype in the real material, on device, using coding agents to turn ideas into working SwiftUI and shipping changes in the codebase alongside engineers. The role is deeply cross-functional. You'll partner closely with iOS, Android, and desktop engineers, product, and fellow designers across the org, and you care about everything that makes a product great: product thinking, interaction, visual craft, copywriting, and engineering. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Lead product design for our iPhone and Android apps, from early concept through polished, shipped detail - Design how the phone works alongside our desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux, so people can start, monitor, steer, and hand off work across devices without friction - Design for agents that work in the background: progress you can glance at, interruptions that respect attention, and clear moments when a person needs to approve, answer, or take over - Make deep use of native platform capabilities, including notifications, Live Activities, widgets, voice, system intents, and extensions, so Perplexity feels built for each device rather than ported to it - Design trust into the product: permissions, approvals, and privacy flows that are clear and honest, and that keep people in control when an agent acts on their behalf - Prototype on device early and often, using real code to answer questions static mocks can't - Use coding agents to build in the production codebase and put up your own PRs, working alongside engineers to close the gap between the design and what ships - Keep patterns consistent across iOS, Android, and desktop while respecting each platform's conventions - Explore what new platform capabilities, input methods, and form factors make possible - Think about how to go from 0→1, and about how your decisions scale as the product grows - Contribute to process so we're always shipping changes you're proud of, as often as possible WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - A strong track record of shipping native mobile apps for consumer or prosumer products - Deep fluency in iOS: platform conventions, navigation patterns, gestures, system components, and what's new each year - Working knowledge of Android and Material conventions, and the judgment to know when a design should adapt across platforms and when it should stay the same - Experience designing products that span multiple devices, or that integrate deeply with operating system features - Excellent interaction, visual, and motion skills, with a sharp eye for detail at small sizes and in glanceable moments - Comfort building with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or similar) to prototype on device and land changes in a production codebase. items.title: Partner Director, EY North America
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s GTM Partnerships team builds a strategic, global partner ecosystem to accelerate customer success, enable responsible enterprise AI adoption, and drive durable growth in support of OpenAI’s mission. We work cross-functionally across Sales, Solutions, Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, Finance, Marketing, Operations, and Customer Success to translate strategic partnerships into measurable outcomes for customers. Global advisory and consulting partners help enterprises move from AI strategy to production deployment. This role will lead OpenAI’s partnership with EY across North America, bringing together EY’s industry, business transformation, technology consulting, and delivery expertise with OpenAI’s products and capabilities. You will turn the global alliance strategy into a focused North America business plan and repeatable field execution that delivers customer and commercial impact. About the Role We are hiring a Partner Director, EY North America to lead OpenAI’s partner business with EY across the region. You will own North America joint business plan, build executive alignment, and activate EY and OpenAI field teams to generate qualified pipeline, win strategic opportunities, and drive successful production adoption. You will align regional priorities and execution with the global EY alliance strategy. This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role. You will connect senior executive engagement with joint account planning, co-selling, solution and delivery alignment, field enablement, governance, and day-to-day execution. items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops silicon and system-level solutions designed for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is responsible for building the next generation of AI-native silicon while working closely with software and research partners to co-design hardware tightly integrated with AI models. In addition to delivering production-grade silicon for OpenAI’s supercomputing infrastructure, the team also creates custom design tools and methodologies that accelerate innovation and enable hardware optimized specifically for AI. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for an experienced Thermal Engineer with 7+ years of experience in thermal management of IT hardware from chip/package to system levels. You’ll work alongside experts in thermal, mechanical, electrical, software, and systems engineering to support the design, analysis, and validation of thermal solutions that ensure the reliability, efficiency, and longevity of mission-critical hardware. This position requires strong analytical skills, hands-on testing experience, and the ability to work in a fast-paced, cross-disciplinary environment. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES - Design and optimize thermal solutions for data center hardware, including chips, power modules, and system-level cooling architectures - Evaluate thermal performance at the chip, package, and board levels, addressing challenges related to power density, heat dissipation, and thermal interface materials - Perform thermal modeling and simulation to predict temperature profiles and identify thermal bottlenecks - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate thermal management strategies into hardware design, from concept to mass production - Support lab testing and validation, including the setup of thermal experiments, data acquisition, and troubleshooting of thermal performance issues - Design and select thermal components, such as cold plates, heat sinks, fans, vapor chambers, and thermal interface materials (TIMs) - Work with firmware and electrical engineers to define and implement thermal control algorithms for dynamic power and cooling management. - Conduct feasibility studies and trade-off analyses to evaluate cooling technologies and improve system thermal efficiency - Partner with suppliers and manufacturers to support the development of custom thermal components and ensure quality in production QUALIFICATIONS - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Thermal Engineering, or a related field (Master’s preferred). - 7+ years of industry experience in thermal design, simulation, and validation for IT hardware - Proficiency in thermal simulation software and CAD tools - Strong understanding of heat transfer principles, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics, with an emphasis on electronics cooling - Hands-on experience with thermal testing equipment, including thermocouples, infrared cameras, wind tunnels, and P-Q characterization setups - Experience in chip/package-level thermal analysis, including die-level heat spreading, and package thermal modeling - Ability to analyze experimental data, identify root causes of thermal issues, and implement corrective actions - Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to perform first-principles calculations to support design decisions. - Self-driven, detail-oriented, and able to work independently or collaboratively in cross-functional engineering environments PREFERRED SKILLS - 10+ years of industry experience in thermal design, simulation, and validation for IT hardware - Extensive experience with data center hardware or high-performance computing systems at scale - Practical experience in developing advanced cooling technologies - Familiarity with thermal control algorithms and dynamic thermal management techniques - items.title: Assistant General Counsel, Derivatives
items.location_text: Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY; Washington, DC
items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Legal team helps Robinhood build and launch products while meeting the rules that apply to a regulated financial company. Our attorneys work alongside Product, Engineering, Compliance and business leaders, giving clear, practical advice on questions that range from new product launches to regulatory matters. We value sound judgment, plain-spoken advice, and a bias toward helping the business move forward the right way. Robinhood is looking for an Assistant General Counsel to join our growing Regulatory legal team. We are looking for an attorney with experience in prediction markets, futures, securities and futures commission merchant/broker-dealer regulatory issues who is excited to work at the intersection of regulation, technology, and finance. We are looking for a highly adaptable and collaborative person who can handle ambiguity and rapidly shifting priorities with flexibility and patience. This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing company and contribute to our mission to democratize finance for all. This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA, New York, NYC and Washington, DC offices, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Navigate complex regulatory frameworks to help the business design innovative financial products and services Identify and draft necessary changes to the firm's systems and procedures to meet the requirements of new rules/regulations Engage with regulators, including CFTC, SEC, NFA and FINRA, and other external parties Draft agreements, policies and procedures, disclosures, account documentation and website materials Resolve account issues related to estates, bankruptcies, powers of attorney, and related matters Monitoring CFTC/NFA, SEC/FINRA and SRO rule developments and making resulting recommendations Research prediction market, futures, securities, and brokerage questions and provide legal analysis and recommendations Partner cross-functionally with teams including litigation, compliance, product, and government affairs What you bring J.D. degree (or foreign equivalent) and membership in at least 1 U.S. state bar 7+ years of legal practice, including in-house experience, specializing in CFTC and/or SEC regulatory law Knowledge or expertise in the rules and regulations relevant to futures commission merchants and/or broker-dealers Track record of developing practical solutions to novel problems Exceptional project management and communication skills Experience at a federal or state financial regulatory agency Experience with technology or start-up organizations, and interest in prediction markets What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career. Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching. Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents. Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more. Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits. Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. For other locations not listed, compensation can be discussed with your recruiter during the interview process. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application. AI Usage Disclosure: Robinhood uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our recruiting process. These tools enhance the efficiency and consistency of our hiring process; however, all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. items.title: Partner Support Operations Lead
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role The Claude Partner Network is how partners build, sell, and deliver on Claude. Partner Support keeps them moving: getting set up, getting certified, registering their work, and understanding where they stand in the program. It runs in layers. Self-serve and an AI support agent handle what they can, an outsourced vendor team works the in-scope (L1) topics, and our specialists take the escalated (L2) cases that need judgment. As our Partner Support Operations Lead, you will run partner support end to end: the team, the operating model, and the systems behind every layer. Partner Programs sets program policy. You will build and run the service levels, knowledge, quality bar, and escalation paths that put that policy into practice, and keep them reliable as volume grows. This is a hands-on operator and builder role. You will be close enough to the queue to know why a case was hard or a rule broke, while you build the team, the vendor coverage, and the Claude-powered automation that keep support from growing in line with partner count. Key responsibilities Manage the partner support team: set priorities and clear expectations, coach the Partner Support Specialists, address performance early, and expand the team if volume or coverage calls for it Own the support operating model: the L1 and L2 boundary, severity definitions, service levels, and escalation paths; review misrouted and wrongly escalated tickets, and fix the rule as well as the ticket Run the L2 queue to its service levels: coverage across shifts, one owner for every case, clean handoffs to the teams that hold the answer, and careful handling of sensitive and high-impact partner issues Manage the support service line with our business process outsourcing (BPO) team: work with their leads day to day and hold a stated quality bar through training and sign-off for each new cohort, the QA rubric and calibration, the weekly operating review, and corrective action when quality or coverage slips Own the knowledge layer: one source of truth for the help center, macros, and AI agent content, updated when a program change ships, so every layer gives partners the same answer from day one of a launch Own the support platform: routing, conversation attributes, views, workflows, access, and service-level reporting; keep the taxonomy short, consistent, and reportable Scale through self-serve, vendors, and Claude: use topic and outcome data to decide what moves to each, and build automations for tagging, routing, QA screening, and reporting; test them on real tickets and add human checkpoints where a wrong answer carries risk Turn what partners ask into fixes: bring the recurring causes behind ticket volume to Partner Programs, Partner Business Systems, and other owners, and follow each one through until the tickets stop Run support on a scorecard covering responsiveness, resolution, escalation accuracy, and quality, and use it to plan capacity and to tell the team, the vendor, and leadership what to fix next Minimum qualifications Support operations experience at a technology company, including managing a small team Experience running an outsourced or BPO support team: onboarding waves, service levels, QA rubrics, calibration, and performance feedback A track record of building a tiered support model from an early stage and running it as volume grew Hands-on depth in Intercom or a comparable platform (Zendesk, Salesforce Service Cloud): routing rules, attributes, workflows, reporting, and permissions Experience running knowledge and content for an AI support agent, including how to review answer quality and close content gaps Strong analytical instincts: able to read ticket data, find the cause behind a spike or a backlog, and turn it into a fix and a capacity plan Sound judgment while the program is still moving: able to make the call with incomplete information, hold a policy line with a frustrated partner or an internal stakeholder, and keep the relationship intact A builder's mindset and clear writing: you use tools like Claude to automate your own work, and you document what you build so a new teammate or vendor lead can run it Preferred qualifications Support operations experience in a B2B, partner, or channel environment Experience supporting a partner, reseller, systems integrator, or independent software vendor (ISV) program Experience building support coverage across regions, time zones, or languages Familiarity with Salesforce, and with the Claude API, Claude Code, or MCP The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $215,000 — $300,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Global Sales Program Manager (SMB Sales)
items.description: About the Role We’re looking for a hands-on sales program manager to build and scale new revenue programs across OpenAI’s global SMB sales teams. Your first focus will be outbound: designing acquisition plays, launching pilots and turning what works into repeatable programs. You’ll combine sales judgment, program management and the ability to drive execution through other teams. Working closely with regional vendor managers, frontline leaders, Enablement, RevOps and product and pricing partners, you’ll bring clarity to what we’re launching, how sellers should execute and how we’ll measure success. In this role, you will: - Build and roll out sales plays: define the audience, targeting, messaging, outreach, qualification and handoff, then work with vendor teams and Enablement to get sellers ready. - Own pilot performance: agree goals and a baseline, review results, diagnose gaps and recommend what to scale, improve or stop. items.title: Tech Lead Manager, Growth Data Science
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Role As part of our growing Data Science and Analytics team, you will play an instrumental role in our company’s mission of building safe and beneficial artificial intelligence by driving data-informed decision making across our organization. You bring experience from high-bar teams and are eager to help shape the norms and best practices of a growing data science team as Anthropic continues to scale. In this unique company, technology, and moment in history, your work will be critical to informing our strategy as we deploy safe, frontier AI at scale to the world. You’ll be the senior data science leader embedded in our Growth team and a strategic thought partner to its product and marketing leads. The Growth team’s job is to keep Anthropic on the exponential by getting more people and companies using and paying for Claude. You’ll help set direction across acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization: bringing a point of view on where to invest, how to grow revenue, and how to deliver more value for our users. As a tech lead manager, you’ll also manage a small team of Product Data Scientists, setting their agenda and raising the bar for how data shapes growth decisions. Key responsibilities Act as a strategic thought partner to Growth product and marketing leads, helping shape growth strategy, roadmap priorities, and the major bets the team makes Set the data science agenda for Growth, deciding where the Product Data Science team can have the most impact and what it should deprioritize Manage and develop a small team of Product Data Scientists Frame the most important and ambiguous questions facing Growth, from where the next users and companies will come from to what makes them stay and pay, size the opportunities, and make clear recommendations, including when they challenge the current direction Define how Growth measures success, establishing the core metrics, guardrails, and measurement frameworks that tie short-term wins to long-term value Set the standard for experimentation and causal inference across Growth, including holdouts and quasi-experimental methods where A/B tests aren’t practical, and personally lead the highest-stakes analyses Guide how Growth measures the return on its programs, including marketing incrementality, LTV, CAC, and payback, and turn the results into budget and channel recommendations Guide the team’s work on targeting and personalization, including how we decide which users get which message, offer, or experience and how we evaluate those decisions Turn complex analyses into clear narratives and recommendations that drive decisions with senior leadership and cross-functional partners Establish foundational data practices and shape the analytics infrastructure Growth needs to support rapid iteration and decision-making as our products grow Minimum qualifications Have extensive experience in data science, including leading analytics for a growth or product area at significant scale Have 5+ years managing data science teams, including setting team direction and developing senior data scientists Have been a trusted partner to senior product, growth, or marketing leaders, with clear examples of changing a roadmap or high-stakes decision Bring strong product sense and business judgment across the growth funnel, including the ability to frame the right question and take a position with incomplete information Have deep expertise in experimental design, causal inference, and statistical modeling at high scale, with enough fluency in Python and SQL to stay hands-on and guide others’ technical work Communicate clearly in writing and in presentations, including to executive audiences Have a bias for action and thrive in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where you must create clarity and drive progress Care about the company’s mission of building helpful, honest, and harmless AI Preferred qualifications Experience measuring marketing incrementality, including holdouts, geo experiments, or marketing mix modeling Experience with targeting, personalization, or uplift models in production Background at consumption-based, multi-product companies serving both consumers and enterprises Experience with AI/ML products or large language models, including using coding agents in your own analytical workflow The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $460,000 — $460,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. Robinhood’s Customer Experience team plays a critical role in Democratizing Finance for All. Our customer experience team supports customers across a wide range of account needs, delivering timely, accurate, and empathetic support across multiple channels. Employees will work either five 8-hour shifts or four 10-hour shifts per week, depending on business needs. Specific schedules will be determined after hire. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. items.title: Resale Operations Lead
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Resellers are a major route for organizations to buy Claude. Our reseller program runs across two motions: hyperscaler resale, where partners resell Claude through the cloud marketplaces (AWS Bedrock today, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry to follow), and direct resale, where partners resell on Anthropic paper through our own quote-to-order and billing systems. Each motion brings its own agreements, systems and cloud counterparts, and the program is expanding across regions at the same time. As our Resale Operations Lead, you will run resale operations: how resellers get authorized, transact, get reported on, get paid and get supported, across both motions and every live cloud. The resale business team sets the strategy and the commercial framework. You will build and run the processes, playbooks and team that put that framework into practice, and keep them reliable as volume grows. This is an operator and builder role, not a partner manager role. You will be hands-on in the detail of a private offer or a partner quote while you build the team, the vendor coverage and the Claude-powered automation that keep resale operations from growing in line with partner count. Reporting to Head of Partner Operations and Systems · San Francisco or New York based What you'll do Lead the resale operations team: set priorities, coach the reseller operations managers, and keep every region on the same playbooks rather than a set of local processes. Build the resale runbook and launch kit across AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft, so that authorizing, onboarding and supporting a reseller works the same way wherever it can, and each new cloud comes online from the kit. Run hyperscaler resale operations: marketplace authorizations and private-offer processing with the cloud alliance teams, and operational escalations with AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft, raised through the cloud alliance teams. Stand up direct resale operations: partner quotes in Salesforce CPQ, order forms, booking and provisioning, and commit tracking and true-ups, working with Deal Desk, Commercial Operations, Finance and Tax. Operate the program rules as controls that can actually run: deal registration to the published policy, eligibility checks, margin and rebate data, and the unauthorized resale process. Flag early what cannot be operated yet. Own the reseller transaction data, so that every reseller transaction traces to an end customer under the attribution rules Partner Strategy and Operations governs, partners are paid accurately and partner-sourced revenue can be measured. Scale through vendors and Claude: propose which resale work moves to outsourced teams or to Claude, run the vendor team's resale scope to a stated quality bar, and build automations with human checkpoints where a wrong decision carries risk. Run resale on a scorecard: application decision time, registration cycle time, attribution coverage, payout accuracy and launch readiness. Use it to tell the team and leadership what to fix next. What might make you a good fit Channel, reseller, distribution or partner operations experience at a technology company, including managing a small team. Hands-on depth in both motions: cloud marketplace resale (authorizations, private offers, deal registration) and direct or contract-based resale (quote-to-order, partner billing). A track record of building a resale or channel operations process from an early stage and running it as volume grew. Fluency in order-to-cash, including Salesforce CPQ or a comparable tool and the Finance, Deal Desk, Legal and Tax coordination that comes with it. Experience managing outsourced or vendor teams: scope, service levels, quality sampling and performance feedback. Sound judgment while the program is still moving. You can make the call with incomplete information, hold a control under pressure from sales or a partner, and keep the relationship intact. A builder's mindset and clear writing. You use tools like Claude to automate your own work, and you document what you build so a new teammate or vendor lead can run it. Strong candidates may also have Experience on the partner or marketplace side of a hyperscaler, or in operations at a major distributor. Experience running partner rebate, margin or incentive operations, or launching a resale program in EMEA or APAC. Familiarity with the Claude API, Claude Code or MCP. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.title: AML Investigator
items.location_text: Denver, CO; New York, NY; Westlake, TX
items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Financial Crimes Investigations team protects Robinhood and its customers by detecting, investigating, and reporting potentially suspicious activity across our brokerage and crypto products. The team partners closely with Compliance, Legal, Product, Risk, and Engineering to strengthen controls and meet regulatory obligations. We focus on thorough investigations, clear documentation, and continuous process improvement to reduce financial crime risk. Our work directly supports regulatory compliance and customer trust. As an AML Investigator, you will conduct complex investigations involving cryptocurrency transactions, brokerage accounts, and cash movement. You will analyze blockchain activity using industry-standard analytics tools, evaluate customer behavior across Robinhood entities, and prepare Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) that meet regulatory requirements. You will manage investigations from initial alert through final decision and documentation, while identifying trends and control enhancements that strengthen our monitoring program. Your analysis will contribute directly to meeting Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) obligations. This role is based in our New York, NY; Denver, CO; or Westlake, TX office(s)office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least [3/4/5] days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Conduct investigations into potentially suspicious activity across cryptocurrency products, brokerage accounts, and fiat transactions generated from transaction monitoring systems, referrals, or external inquiries. Analyze blockchain transactions using tools such as Chainalysis, TRM, or similar platforms to trace fund flows and identify indicators of money laundering or other financial crimes. Review customer activity across Robinhood Financial, Robinhood Securities, Robinhood Crypto, and Robinhood Money to assess risk and determine appropriate case outcomes. Draft clear, well-supported Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) that meet regulatory standards and internal quality benchmarks. Manage the full lifecycle of investigations, including alert review, evidence gathering, decisioning, documentation, and case closure. Contribute to process improvements by identifying trends, control gaps, or tooling enhancements that improve investigative quality and efficiency. What you bring 2+ years of AML investigation experience within a broker-dealer, cryptocurrency firm, fintech company, or financial institution, including SAR drafting. Hands-on experience analyzing cryptocurrency transactions and using blockchain analytics platforms (e.g., Chainalysis, TRM, or similar tools). Preference for those with course certifications from Chainalysis or TRM Experience working across both fiat and crypto product environments Strong understanding of BSA/AML regulatory requirements, particularly as they relate to virtual currencies and digital asset platforms. Ability to evaluate large data sets, document findings clearly, and make defensible risk-based decisions. Bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice, Finance, Economics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Preference for those with ACAMS certification or Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) designation. What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. For other locations not listed, compensation can be discussed with your recruiter during the interview process. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application. AI Usage Disclosure: Robinhood uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our recruiting process. These tools enhance the efficiency and consistency of our hiring process; however, all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. The team comprises Sales, Solutions, Support, Marketing, and Partnership professionals who collaborate to create valuable solutions that will help bring AI to as many users as possible. This role combines technical understanding, strategic vision, relationship management, and value-driven sales strategy tailored specifically to Intelligence Community customers. You’ll drive key opportunities throughout the full sales cycle, from pipeline generation through deployment and expansion. You’ll collaborate closely with researchers, engineers, solution strategists, and cross-functional partners to help Intelligence Community customers advance their missions through AI. This role is based in Washington, D.C. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In addition, this role requires frequent on-site engagement at customer and partner facilities across the Washington, D.C./Northern Virginia corridor, including classified environments. In this role, you will: - Manage a focused set of key U.S. Intelligence Community accounts, developing and executing comprehensive account strategies. - Lead Intelligence Community customers through their AI adoption journey, from initial consideration through successful deployment and expansion. - Experience partnering with federal systems integrators and specialized mission partners on capture strategies, co-selling, and program expansion. - Proven experience selling cloud, cybersecurity, hybrid-cloud, or AI infrastructure into sensitive or classified environments, including on-premises and air-gapped deployment patterns. - Consistently delivering growth in fast-paced, high-performance environments. - Working directly with senior Intelligence Community executives, mission leaders, technical stakeholders, and decision-makers. - Deep relationships and native familiarity with Intelligence Community missions, organizational structures, workflows, and buying processes. - Translating technical capabilities into clear mission outcomes and strategic value. - Communicating technical and strategic concepts clearly to both Intelligence Community customers and internal stakeholders. - Leading high-visibility customer briefings, executive engagements, demonstrations, and industry events. - Gathering, distilling, and applying detailed market intelligence, including agency priorities, policy developments, budget trends, acquisition strategies, and competitor activity. You might thrive in this role if you: - Are customer-centric. You are motivated to deeply understand defense customers’ priorities and help them achieve their mission-critical objectives using AI. You embrace the opportunity to help deploy OpenAI’s technology in ways that advance national security missions and benefit humanity. You’re enthusiastic about educating defense customers on AI capabilities and strategic implications. - Are a builder. You enjoy impacting how our company grows its defense and intelligence business. You excel in establishing robust systems and processes tailored to defense customer requirements, executing them with precision and agility. - Are excited by new challenges. You thrive when solving complex, mission-critical defense and national security problems. Bespoke challenges requiring multidimensional knowledge excite you, and you’re eager to experiment with innovative solutions within national security environments. - Are a strategist.
